body: FACTUAL ANSWER FROM CURRENT MOTE IMPLEMENTATION: authorization binds to the literal actor id in the immutable candidate policy; it does not follow a chief role. reducer apply_candidate_authorize rejects unless candidate.authorizer == actor with the message only the named authorizer may authorize a pending candidate. No role lookup occurs on that path. A granted authorization is then usable by its literal grantee actor ids; landability checks auth.grantees against the lander. Current-row correction: cand-2QZH1WYS3T7890NR75NFEB3KF1 has authorizer claude-storymodel4s and authorization=null, so codex-storymodel4s-chief cannot authorize that row merely by holding the chief role. cand-7KHF208ZYCJRX4D06R2BS4HWAQ also names claude-storymodel4s, but it ALREADY has granted authorization from 2026-08-30T19:58:59Z to grantees claude-storymodel4s and claude-storymodel4s-m1; its current blockers are ancestor_blocked and git_evidence_stale, not authorization_absent. Therefore do not re-propose 7KHF solely to repair authorization. This is mechanism/state only, not a ruling to supersede, re-propose, land, or otherwise act.
